evals.prompt: Write a developer guide for this repository so new engineers can onboard, and give us a printable PDF too.
evals.expected_output: Reads the repo's agent and contribution rules, builds a fact sheet with path:line sources and counted numbers, plans four parts, writes the home page, chapters and glossary from the templates, finds and credits a public-domain cover plate, builds the PDF, Word file and cover image, and verifies every page.
expectations: Builds a fact sheet before writing, with a source for each claim and a command for each number
Uses the four-part structure and the chapter anatomy (In this chapter, lead, sections, Check yourself, nav)
Chooses a cover plate from the subject and records its credit and licence
Builds with build.sh and reviews the pages with contact sheets before reporting

evals.prompt: Our guide's cover looks like cheap clip art. Make it look like a real developer book.
evals.expected_output: Reads cover.md, explains what professional technical covers do, searches open collections with find_plate.py for a plate tied to the project's name or craft, shows candidates as a contact sheet, previews with make_cover.py --preview, and never uses stock illustration or a publisher's trade dress.
expectations: Proposes a real public-domain plate tied to the subject rather than an illustration of the UI
Shows two or three candidates and recommends one
Records the plate's credit for the back cover
Does not imitate a specific publisher's trade dress

evals.prompt: We have three related repos (a service, its plugins and its SDK). Can their guides feel like one set?
evals.expected_output: Makes them volumes of one series: the same cover.series, Volume I/II/III, one plate per volume from one family of subjects, one colour per volume starting from the brand colour, and checks the covers side by side.
expectations: Uses a shared series name and volume numbers in each repo's .print.json
Picks plates from one family of subjects
Gives each volume its own colour, starting from the brand colour
Writes each guide in its own repository and cross-references instead of duplicating

evals.prompt: Generate an OpenAPI reference for our endpoints.
evals.expected_output: Recognises an API reference request, which this skill excludes, and does not write a textbook-style guide for it; suggests generating reference docs from the schema instead.
expectations: Does not start the developer-guide workflow for a pure API reference
Points to generated reference documentation instead
